issues.what: The follow-up's SPA re-run did not remove the near-benchmark variant it was meant to remove. FINDINGS states '0 of 1568 candidates excluded ... every grid variant's selection gain is non-zero in every active session (no variant applies the Foundation's next-CHoCH exit, so every variant differs from the benchmark wherever a session has a trade)'. That is true only at the harness's 1e-9 INR activity threshold: the variant `stop foundation / scale none / trail none / time_stop None / choch True` is, in substance, the Foundation L1 exit (the next CHoCH after an entry is always against the position), and its per-session selection gain exceeds 0.05 INR in only 7 of 578 sessions (minute, exit-ledger id 0c142743f6d7b0bd) and 1 of 408 (5minute, id ea2c65c77b1f3eda; its inert-key twin `time_stop 120`, id 807549ccd89a4d42, is identical). The other sessions carry |gain| ~ 1e-3 INR: float noise between lab.manage's arithmetic and l1_net_inr (the parity check tolerates 0.005 per trade), which the 1e-9 test counts as 'active'. So the studentised SPA p reported in sections 3, 9 and 10 (0.396 minute, 0.4965 5minute; all-trials 0.3965 / 0.4825) is still inflated by exactly the candidate the harness revision targeted, and the stated reason for '0 excluded' is false.

issues.evidence: Reproduced with harness.spa on the study's own vectors and tags (same bootstrap draws): minute C family studentised SPA p 0.396 / RC 0.501 -> 0.322 / 0.448 with the one near-degenerate variant dropped; all-trials 0.3965 -> 0.314. 5minute C family 0.4965 / 0.5175 -> 0.185 / 0.21; all-trials 0.4825 -> 0.1685. Unstudentised p unchanged (0.5405 / 0.1505), best candidate and best t unchanged (785, t 1.683; 1025, t 2.761). Mechanism confirmed by replicating the harness internals: the near-degenerate variant is the argmax of the studentised bootstrap family max in 19.8% (minute) and 37.9% (5minute) of the 2000 draws, with |t_b| up to 9,186 and 19,152 (its bootstrap sd collapses to noise when its few substantive sessions are not drawn). Substantive-activity counts at |gain| > 0.05, 1.0 and 5.0 INR agree (1 variant below min-active on minute, 2 on 5minute); at 1e-9 every variant reads 578/578 and 408/408, with 50,382 (minute) and 138,178 (5minute) cells in 1e-9 < |gain| < 0.01. The verdict is not affected: the corrected p values (0.322, 0.185; all-trials 0.314, 0.1685) still fail spa_p <= 0.10, and the minute C nested pick and learner B also fail diff_top1_gains_removed > 0; the null result stands.
issues.fix: The study may not edit harness.py, so: (1) replace the FINDINGS/findings.json statement with the measured facts: the min-active rule at 1e-9 excludes nothing because the vectors carry ~1e-3 INR float noise; at any substantive threshold (>= 0.05 INR) the Foundation-stop + CHoCH-against variant (and its 5-min time_stop-120 twin) is near-degenerate (7/578, 1/408 active) and inflates the studentised p; report both the harness's p and the p with those candidates excluded (0.322 / 0.185; all-trials 0.314 / 0.1685), naming the rule and the ids, and keep the unstudentised p beside them. (2) Make the study's vectors exact so the harness rule works as written: in exlib.session_vectors / 01_c_grid, snap a variant's per-trade net to the Foundation net when the exit bar and fill coincide (c_grid_check already verifies exit_bar matches), or round per-trade nets to the paisa before summing, then re-run 05_evaluate.py (no learner rerun needed). (3) Ask the harness owner to raise the activity threshold in harness.spa to a monetary tolerance (e.g. |d| > 0.01 INR) so the fix cannot be defeated by arithmetic noise; the 05_evaluate.py mirror at line 78 should follow it. Verdict text ('no candidate' on all six lines, null result) can stand once the numbers are corrected.
